doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Rock and roll, brushes, and playing rock tunes with his drummer
summary: He finds rock disorganized, tells of a drummer scorning brushes, and describes playing blues/rock with a versatile drummer.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: How did rock & roll affect your employment as a musician?
Well I’ll tell you about rock & roll. I can’t say I have the greatest respect for it because a lot of times it’s very disorganized, the music that is.
I never heard that sort of term.

I don’t know, a lot of the guys that play it don’t seem to have, you know like you talk to a jazz musician and you talk to a rock musician. And some of these young guys man, the ideas they have you wouldn’t believe it. One guy told me he said, “Brushes, I don’t use no God damn brushes, man. Brushes, that’s for idiots.” I said, “Well how do you go and work?” I said, “You ain’t going to work too much, man.” Because brushes are an important part of drums. “How are you going to work?”
That’s such a simple statement, it’s so important. Because sometimes people don’t take that into account.
Well yeah. I said, “Man you ain’t going to work too much, too often.” That’s an important part of the drums. And some guys that play them play them very well, very good at it.
When you were leading your own band and playing gigs if people came up and requested a current rock tune or something, what did you do?

Well you know sometimes, sometimes we could play it because I had a drummer working with me, Richard — aw I forget the man’s last name. Anyway, he could play Dixieland, he could play rock, he could play jazz, blues. He knew that God damn drumset

so good and knew the rhythms. That’s the important thing. He knew those rhythms and he would play them and play them comfortable. So if they asked for a rock tune, what I would do, I had some blues/rock things with the background, and I would play them. “Oh yeah, you played rock.” I said, “Yeah, we play rock.”
Yeah. Like Ramsey Lewis was playing rock. You know? He just took songs and sort of put a rock beat to it.

The man was a hell of a pianist. Yeah. There’s really nothing difficult, but the main thing is the rhythm. If you’re a pianist or you are a drummer or a bass player and you have that rhythm in your mind, you feel it you know, you can play it. Because it’s music, it’s compatible music. When you figure it all out it’s music.
